modules.title: Past & plans
modules.summary: Say what you did, what you will do, what you must and can do.

lessons.title: Did it, done it, not yet
intro: Plain verb + တယ် can already mean past, and time words like မနေ့က 'yesterday' usually do the work. To make the past clear, add ခဲ့ (gḛ): သွားခဲ့တယ် 'I went'.
Verb + ပြီးပြီ (pyí bì) means 'already done'. For 'not yet', wrap the verb in မ … သေးဘူး: မစားရသေးဘူး 'I haven't eaten yet'.

lessons.title: Plans & must
intro: You already know မယ် (mè) for the future and ချင်တယ် (jìn dè) for 'want to'. Add တော့ before မယ် for 'about to, right now': စားတော့မယ် 'I'm going to eat now'.
ရ (ya̰) after a verb means 'have to': သွားရမယ် 'I have to go'. Say it when you need to leave a family visit.

lessons.title: Have you ever…?
intro: ဖူး (hpú) after a verb means 'have ever done'. ရောက်ဖူးလား 'have you ever been (there)?' is a favourite question for visitors.
For 'never', use the usual negative: မ + verb + ဖူးဘူး. After an open syllable ဖူး usually sounds like bú.

lessons.title: Can & can't
intro: Burmese has two words for 'can'. နိုင် (nàin) is being able to or having the chance: လာနိုင်တယ် 'I can come'. တတ် (daʔ) is a learned skill: ရေကူးတတ်တယ် 'I can swim'.
To ask permission, use verb + လို့ရလား: ထိုင်လို့ရလား 'Can I sit?'

modules.title: Opinions & small talk
modules.summary: Share what you think, react, compliment the food and chat about the weather.

lessons.title: I think, I like
intro: ထင်တယ် (htìn dè) 'I think' goes at the end, after the opinion: ကောင်းမယ် ထင်တယ် 'I think it'll be good'.
ကြိုက်တယ် is 'like'. Put အရမ်း (ə-yán) 'very' in front to make it stronger.

lessons.title: Good, beautiful, fun
intro: Describing words work like verbs: လှတယ် 'is beautiful', ကောင်းတယ် 'is good'. Make them negative the same way: မကောင်းဘူး 'not good'.
စရာကောင်းတယ် after a verb means 'worth doing': ပျော်စရာကောင်းတယ် 'it's fun'.

lessons.title: Me too & agreeing
intro: လည်း (lé) after a word means 'too, also': ကျွန်မလည်း ကြိုက်တယ် 'I like it too'.
Burmese conversation avoids flat disagreement. မထင်ဘူး 'I don't think so' or ဖြစ်နိုင်တယ် 'maybe' are gentle ways to disagree.

lessons.title: Compliments & weather
intro: Praising the food is the best compliment you can give at a family meal. Say it often!
Weather is easy small talk: Yangon is usually hot or rainy. ဒီနေ့ 'today' + အရမ်းပူတယ် 'really hot' will always get a reply.

items.my: သွားခဲ့တယ်
items.note: ခဲ့ (gḛ) after a verb makes it clearly past. After a checked syllable it's said hkḛ.

items.my: မနေ့က
မနေ့က ဘယ်သွားလဲ
items.note: No past marker needed: မနေ့က 'yesterday' already sets the time.
Verb + ပြီးပြီ (pyí bì) = already done.

items.my: မစားရသေးဘူး
items.note: မ + verb + (ရ)သေးဘူး = not yet. The answer to 'Have you eaten?' when you haven't.

items.my: မနက်ဖြန်
မနက်ဖြန် ဘာလုပ်မလဲ
စားတော့မယ်
items.note: တော့မယ် (da̰w mè) = about to, going to right now.

items.my: သွားရမယ်
items.note: Verb + ရမယ် (ya̰ mè) = have to / must.

items.my: အလုပ်လုပ်ရမယ်
မြန်မာပြည် သွားချင်တယ်
items.en: I want to go to Myanmar

items.my: မသွားလည်း ရပါတယ်
items.note: မ + verb + လည်း ရတယ် = it's fine not to…
ရောက် (yauʔ) = arrive, get to. Verb + ပြီ = it has happened now.

items.my: ပုဂံ ရောက်ဖူးလား
items.en: Have you ever been to Bagan?
items.note: Verb + ဖူး (hpú) = have ever done it.

items.my: တစ်ခါ ရောက်ဖူးတယ်
မရောက်ဖူးဘူး
items.note: မ + verb + ဖူးဘူး = have never.
After an open syllable ဖူး is usually voiced: bú.

items.my: လာနိုင်တယ်
items.note: Verb + နိုင်တယ် = can (be able to, have the chance).

items.my: မလာနိုင်ဘူး
ထမင်းချက်တတ်လား
items.note: Verb + တတ် = know how to (a learned skill). After a checked syllable it's taʔ, otherwise daʔ.

items.my: ရေမကူးတတ်ဘူး

items.note: Verb + လို့ရလား = may I…? / is it OK to…?

items.my: ထင်တယ်
ကောင်းမယ် ထင်တယ်
items.note: The opinion comes first, ထင်တယ် 'I think' comes last.

items.my: ဘယ်လို ထင်လဲ
အရမ်းကြိုက်တယ်
items.note: အရမ်း (ə-yán) = very, really.

Verb + ရမယ် = have to / must.
Verb + နိုင်တယ် = can, be able to.

scenarios.title: Last weekend, next weekend
scenarios.role: Your partner's cousin, a friendly woman in her twenties from Yangon
scenarios.setup: You're chatting over tea. Ask the learner simple questions about what they did yesterday or last weekend, what they're doing tomorrow, whether they've ever been to places in Myanmar (Bagan, Mandalay, Inle Lake) or tried Burmese foods (mohinga, tea-leaf salad), and what they can do (cook, swim, speak Burmese). Use simple colloquial Burmese with ခဲ့, ပြီးပြီ, မ…သေးဘူး, မယ်, ရမယ်, ဖူး, နိုင်, တတ်. Keep sentences short.

scenarios.title: Small talk at dinner
scenarios.role: Your partner's father, a warm, chatty man in his sixties
scenarios.setup: The learner is having dinner at the family's home in Yangon. Ask whether they like the food, what they think of Yangon and Myanmar, chat about the hot or rainy weather, and ask why they're learning Burmese. React warmly to compliments. Use simple colloquial Burmese and short sentences; give the learner chances to say I think, I like, me too, it's beautiful, it's delicious.

reading.title: Read: Past & plans
intro: Look for the little words after the verb: ခဲ့ (past), ပြီ (already), ရ (must), နိုင် (can), ဖူး (ever).

reading.title: Read: Opinions & small talk
intro: Short sentences you'll say at every family meal. Spot the negative frame မ … ဘူး.

uncertain.why: Voicing of ဖူး after an open syllable: written bú (as commonly heard), but some speakers keep hpú. Check with partner.
Same ဖူး voicing question (sá bú lá vs sá hpú lá).
Voicing in စိတ်ဝင်စား (wìn zá vs wìn sá) not fully certain.
Whether တူ is voiced (tù vs dù) in သဘောတူတယ် in normal speech.
ချစ်သူ means boyfriend/girlfriend; for a spouse, the learner may prefer ကျွန်တော့်မိန်းမ / ကျွန်မယောက်ျား (my wife/husband). Also check ချစ်သူ့ (creaky possessive) spelling.
Both မစားရသေးဘူး and မစားသေးဘူး are used; chose the version with ရ. Confirm which sounds more natural to the family.
